details.biography:
The Broken Anvil · Level 1 - The Recruits · Seat 4, Ranged

A white-haired Nu'Dravi who struck a bargain with the Queen of Air and Darkness, and throws purple eldritch force like she was born to it. Poised, sardonic and hard to read; she is comfortable in the dark in ways that make the others uneasy. The Keepers ask fewer questions than anyone else, which suits her perfectly.

Tonight: Her first proper job for the Keepers, and the dark under a mountain feels like home.

In a fight

Hang back and Eldritch Blast every turn (Reflex DC 13; 1d6+2 on a failure). Daze the goblin who matters, drop Sleep on a pack before it reaches you, and Fey Step out of reach.
details.backgroundStory:
Abilities

Eldritch Blast. At will, 60ft, one creature: Reflex save DC 13. On a failure 1d6+2 force (+2 from Cantrip Mastery); on a success half of 1d6. Never uses a slot.

Spell Use. Arcane caster, Charisma-based, save DC 13. Two 1st-level slots a day (1, +1 for Charisma 13+), back after a long rest. You know Faerie Fire (Path spell) and Sleep. No spell attack rolls: harmful spells call for a save. Any armour or shield blocks your casting. Her staff is her focus.

Fey Step (Path of the Fey). Once per round, teleport up to 10ft to an unoccupied space you can see as part of your movement.

Dark Gift (The Queen of Air and Darkness). Darkness you create is impenetrable to all sight, darkvision included. You see perfectly in any darkness, magical or mundane.

Pact. A Warlock holds the patron's alignment, so her Allegiance is the Queen's, whatever her Outlook.

Nu'Dravi. Speed 30ft, darkvision 120ft. Immune to magical sleep. Advantage on saves against charm, and on Perception by sight or hearing in low light or darkness. Trance: 4 hours' rest.

Innate magic. Dancing Lights at will. Once a day, Darkness (20ft radius, 1 round at her level) or Faerie Fire (Reflex save, DC 13).

Sunlight. She follows no faith: Disadvantage on attacks and sight-based Perception for the first hour of direct sunlight each day.

Cantrip Mastery (1st, Arcane & Devout). Two extra cantrips (Daze, Mage Hand). Once per round, add your Charisma modifier (+2) to a cantrip's damage when it hits or the target fails its save.

Casting

Eldritch Blast (cantrip): 60ft, one creature, Reflex DC 13; 1d6+2 force on a failure (Cantrip Mastery), half of 1d6 on a success.

Daze (cantrip, Cantrip Mastery): 60ft, one humanoid of Level 4 or lower is Stunned for 1 round; Will negates, and it is then immune to your Daze for the encounter.

Mage Hand (cantrip, Cantrip Mastery): 30ft, 1 minute; an invisible hand moves an unattended object of up to 5 lb at 15ft a round.

Faerie Fire (1st, Path spell): 60ft, 20ft radius, 1 minute; creatures are outlined, lose Invisible and concealment, and attacks against them have Advantage; Reflex negates.

Sleep (1st): 90ft, 15ft radius; 2d4+1 Levels of creatures fall Unconscious for 1d4 minutes, lowest Level first; Will negates, damage wakes them, and Level 5+, undead and constructs are unaffected.

Armour Class on the sheet: 10 + 2 (Dex); no armour or shield (Warlocks are trained in none, and wearing any blocks casting) = 12

IdentityA pact-bound caster whose patron answers with servants, invocations and dark gifts, and always wants something back.

Spell Slot Progression

Class Abilities

1st Level

Eldritch Blast

  • Effect: At will, as your action, blast one creature within 60ft (V, S).
  • It makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC, taking force damage on a failure or half on a success. No slot required.
  • The damage is 1d8, 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 11th and 4d8 at 17th, with no ability bonus.
  • Eldritch Blast is a class feature, not a spell on the Warlock list.
  • Signature blast: when you cast Eldritch Blast you may spend 1 Patron Favour to make it your signature blast: apply up to one Shape and one Mark you know (see Eldritch Invocations). Each creature makes one save against the blast, its Shape and its Mark together.
  • Path mark: you know your Path's Mark without spending an invocation: Infernal Hellfire, Abyss Dread, Fey Grasping, Great Old One Withering.
  • Disadvantage: any Warlock may spend 1 Patron Favour as part of casting Eldritch Blast: one target makes its save against it with Disadvantage. This costs its own Favour.

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast arcane spells using your slots.
  • Each time you unlock a slot level you gain three spells of that level: your Path spell (see Patron Paths), your Pact spell (see Pacts), both always known, and one spell of your choice from the Warlock list in Spellcasting in Arneyan.
  • You may cast any spell you know with any slot of its level or higher.
  • Slots are shared with Pact Summons: see Spell Slot Progression above.
  • Cantrips: you know two cantrips of your choice from the Warlock list, and learn one more at 5th, 9th and 13th level.
  • Swapping: when you gain a Warlock level you may swap one chosen spell for another of the same level.

Path, Patron and Pact

  • Effect: You choose a Path, a patron within it and a Pact (see Patron Paths and Pacts). Your Path gives its passive and one gift; your patron its boon; your Pact its frame, its core feature and two invocations.

Patron Favour

  • Effect: Your patron's power is one pool of favour: 1 use a day at 1st level, 2 at 4th and 3 at 8th. Spend a use on your signature blast, a Path gift, an Eldritch Strike or anything else that costs Patron Favour; a power that is always on costs nothing.
  • When you spend your last Patron Favour of the day, the GM may name a small service your patron expects before it returns.

2nd Level

Eldritch Invocations

  • Effect: Choose one invocation from the list in Eldritch Invocations, below.
  • Choose another at 4th, 6th, 9th and 15th level, on top of the two your Pact gives at 1st. When you gain a Warlock level you may swap one invocation for another.
  • You cannot take the same invocation twice.

3rd Level

Pact Summons

  • Effect: Your patron sends a servant.
    • Every summons expends a slot of the creature's tier (Tier 1 = 1st level, Tier 2 = 2nd, Tier 3 = 3rd, Tier 4 = 5th).
    • A ritual summons takes 10 minutes and lasts 1 hour; a combat summons uses your action and lasts 1 minute.
    • Full stat blocks are in Monsters & Treasure, but summons use the stats in your Path's Shared Summons table, not the Bestiary's.
    • Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 servants, and the Erinyes and Treant in Tier 4, have double the HP and damage dice of their stat blocks, and the tables below already show them doubled.
    • A servant saves as a creature of its Level.
  • The creature does not roll initiative: it acts immediately after you each round, moving and taking one action (all its listed attacks together count as that action). It obeys your spoken commands; with none, it attacks the nearest visible enemy.
  • One summon active at a time (the Pact of the Chain allows two from 9th). It departs when its duration ends, when you dismiss it with a word or when slain; a slain summon cannot be called again until you finish a long rest.
  • If you fall unconscious, your summon only defends itself until you wake or it departs.
  • Bound Servant: once a day, a combat summons of your highest tier costs no slot. From 10th level, twice a day.

4th Level

  • Patron Favour: 2 uses a day

7th Level

Dark Harvest

  • Effect: Once per encounter, when you reduce a creature to 0 HP or below, recover one expended spell slot of a level up to half that creature's Level (rounded up, minimum 1st level). It must be a foe that fought your side this encounter, not helpless, and not summoned, created or controlled by your side.
  • Example: kill a Level 6 creature, recover up to a 3rd level slot

8th Level

  • Second Path gift: choose one more gift from your Path's four.
  • Patron Favour: 3 uses a day

10th Level

Patron's Hand

  • Effect: Once per encounter, one Path gift, signature blast or Eldritch Strike costs no Patron Favour. Bound Servant works twice a day.

Renown: Name

  • Effect: Your deeds are known. Title: A name your patron gives you. Cultists, hedge-witches and the desperate know the signs: you have Advantage on Reaction Checks with them and with anyone who fears your patron. Your first follower, a devotee, joins you.

13th Level

Patron's Whisper

  • Effect: During a long rest, commune directly with your patron to ask one yes-or-no question. The answer is always truthful, though the patron's understanding of truth may not align with yours.

15th Level

Pact Summons (Tier 4)

  • Effect: Your patron's most powerful servant becomes available. Tier 4 summons expend a 5th level slot, whether ritual or combat.

The Pact Deepens

  • Effect: A Path gift that deals damage rolls half as many dice again (round down). This doesn't change Eldritch Blast or its Marks.

Patron Surge

  • Effect: Choose one 7th-level Wizard spell. Once per day you can cast it without a slot; you take 7d6 damage that nothing can reduce.
  • Charisma Bonus: gain a permanent +1 to Charisma. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).
  • Renown: Holding: you may found a hidden sanctum as your Holding (see Your Holding (15th) in Keeps & Kingdoms).
  • Your Pact improves, as it says.

17th Level

Envoy of the Patron

  • Effect: Creatures of your patron's kind (devils, demons, fey or aberrations) parley with you before fighting, and you can bargain with them for safe passage or secrets.

20th Level

Eldritch Master

  • Effect: Once per day, spend 1 minute communing with your patron to immediately recover all expended spell slots. The patron always wants something in return: the GM sets the price, such as a service, a named soul or a year of the cult's tithe.

Renown: Cult

  • Effect: Your stronghold becomes your cult or cabal (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 followers and one 1st-level Warlock of your Path join it. While you hold it, your patron grants you one extra use of Patron Favour a day.

Patron Paths

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Warlock folder. Drag one onto your character.

  • Choose a Path at character creation.
  • Each Path gives a passive, a menu of combat gifts, Path spells and a shared summon pool.
  • Within it choose your patron (your kit): it shapes your patron boon, one out-of-combat gift, and its lore.
  • Your Path's gifts reshape what your Patron Favour buys.
  • Path gifts: pick one of your Path's first two gifts at 1st level, and one more of its four at 8th. Each costs 1 Patron Favour unless it says otherwise, and takes your action unless it says otherwise.

Path of the Infernal

The Nine Hells run on hierarchy, contracts, and hellfire. Every devil serves the chain above them. Every Infernal Warlock serves that chain whether they know it or not. Its archdevils are Lawful Evil, and their tongue is Infernal.

  • Path Passive, Hellfire Affinity: Resistance 5 to fire damage. Treat all 1s on fire damage dice as 2s.

Path Gifts

  • Hellfire Rebuke (1st): once per round, out of turn, when a creature damages you, it takes 2d10 fire damage, +1d10 per 6 Warlock levels, no save.
  • Binding Contract (1st): a creature within 60ft makes a Will save. On a failure it can't attack you or target you with a spell until the end of its next turn, and it answers one question you ask truthfully.
  • Ice Tomb (8th): a creature within 60ft makes a Fortitude save or is Paralysed in ice for 1 minute, with Resistance to all damage but fire while encased. It saves again at the end of each of its turns.
  • Fallen Light (8th): a 30ft-radius burst on a point within 60ft, sparing creatures you choose. Undead and fiends take 8d8 radiant damage, others 4d8 fire; Reflex halves.

Path Spells

  • One Path spell per slot level, gained when that slot level is unlocked (alongside your chosen Warlock-list spell of the same level).
  • Cast it with any slot of that level or higher; a Path spell is always treated as the slot level shown in the table, even where the Master list gives it a different level.
  • Slots are shared with summoning: a slot spent on a summon can't also be used to cast.

Path of the Abyss

Pure chaos, destruction, and primal evil. Demons don't negotiate: they unmake. Its demon lords are Chaotic Evil, and their tongue is Abyssal.

  • Path Passive, Abyssal Resilience: Immunity to poison damage and the poisoned condition. Advantage on saves vs disease.

Path Gifts

  • Raise the Fallen (1st, no Favour): a creature you kill with Eldritch Blast, a cantrip or a spell rises as a zombie at the start of your next turn. One at a time; it counts as one of your servants.
  • Maddening Gaze (1st): a creature within 60ft makes a Will save or is Terrified until the end of its next turn (it doesn't have to flee); on a natural 1, it is also Stunned.
  • Bestial Fury (8th): for the encounter, the first attack against you each round has Disadvantage, and you can't be Charmed or Frightened. You can't cast spells with slots while it lasts; Eldritch Blast still works.
  • The Hunt (8th): mark a creature within 120ft for the encounter. You know where it is; one damaging spell or blast of yours each round deals +2d6 to it; and once during the encounter, when it would drop you to 0 HP, you drop to 1 instead.

Path Spells

  • One Path spell per slot level, gained when that slot level is unlocked (alongside your chosen Warlock-list spell of the same level).
  • Cast it with any slot of that level or higher; a Path spell is always treated as the slot level shown in the table, even where the Master list gives it a different level.
  • Slots are shared with summoning: a slot spent on a summon can't also be used to cast.

Path of the Fey

The Feywild runs on heightened emotion, ancient bargains, and beauty that kills if you stare too long. Tiandra is Chaotic Good, Verenestra Chaotic Neutral and the Queen of Air and Darkness Chaotic Evil; their tongue is Sylvan.

  • Path Passive, Fey Step: Once per round, teleport up to 10ft to a visible unoccupied space as part of your movement.

Path Gifts

  • Shadow Step (1st): step into a shadow within 10ft and out of another within 60ft. You may take one willing creature beside you along.
  • Summer's Fury (1st): once per round, when a creature within 30ft fails a save against a damaging effect of yours, every die of that effect against it counts as its highest.
  • Unseelie Shroud (8th): a creature within 60ft makes a Will save or for 1 minute is Blinded, has its speed halved and has Disadvantage on saves; it saves again at the end of each of its turns. This doesn't apply to an effect that kills outright.
  • Wild Growth (8th): a 20ft radius on a point within 60ft. Each enemy there makes a Fortitude save or is Restrained, saving again at the end of each of its turns.

Path Spells

  • One Path spell per slot level, gained when that slot level is unlocked (alongside your chosen Warlock-list spell of the same level).
  • Cast it with any slot of that level or higher; a Path spell is always treated as the slot level shown in the table, even where the Master list gives it a different level.

Something that was never meant to be touched. The pact wasn't negotiated: it was noticed. Bolothamogg and Tharizdun are Chaotic Evil, and their tongue is Deep Speech.

Once a round, as part of your action, you can force your mind on one unwilling creature in range: it makes a Will save against your Class Save DC or is Shaken until the end of its next turn.

Path Gifts

  • Unravel (1st): a creature or object within 30ft takes 1d10 necrotic damage, +1d10 per 4 Warlock levels (Fortitude halves), and attacks against it have Advantage until the end of your next turn.
  • The Truth Beneath (1st): you gain True Seeing for 1 minute.
  • Far Realm Rift (8th): a 20ft radius on a point within 60ft. Each creature there makes a Will save or is Stunned for 1 round and takes 4d8 psychic damage. The rift lingers one round: a creature that enters it or starts its turn there saves again.
  • Eye of Bolothamogg (8th): an eye (AC 15, 30 HP) appears within 60ft for 3 rounds. On each of your turns it fires a ray at a creature it can see: 4d6 force damage, Reflex halves. A creature it kills is disintegrated.

  • One Path spell per slot level, gained when that slot level is unlocked (alongside your chosen Warlock-list spell of the same level).
  • Cast it with any slot of that level or higher; a Path spell is always treated as the slot level shown in the table, even where the Master list gives it a different level.

Pacts

  • Choose one Pact at character creation: how you fight.
  • Each Pact gives a frame and a core feature at 1st level, two invocations free at 1st, a step at 7th, an improvement at 9th and a big step at 15th.
  • Your Pact spells are always known, one per slot level, gained as you unlock that level (Level 1, 3, 7, 11, 15 and 19).

Eldritch Invocations

(Level) = the earliest level you can take it. Blade invocations are for the Pact of the Blade only, except Life Drinker.

Shapes (for your signature blast)

  • Lance: a 60ft line, 5ft wide.
  • Burst (6th): a 10ft radius on a point within 60ft.
  • Chain (6th): the target and one more creature within 30ft of it; from 11th level, two more.
  • Long: range 120ft, and the blast ignores half and three-quarters cover.

Marks (for your signature blast; each lands on a failed save)

  • Agonising: the blast deals your Charisma modifier twice more damage, and the target takes full damage even if it saves.
  • Repelling: a Large or smaller target is pushed 15ft away from you (in a Burst, away from its centre).
  • Hellfire: it takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its turns (2d6 from 11th level). The fire ends when it or a creature beside it spends an action to put it out, or after 1 minute.
  • Grasping: its speed is 0 until the end of its next turn.
  • Draining: you gain temporary HP equal to the damage dealt.
  • Dread: it is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn.
  • Binding: until the end of its next turn it can't teleport, turn invisible or change shape, and an invisible creature becomes visible.
  • Withering: it has Disadvantage on its next save against one of your spells before the end of your next turn. This doesn't apply to a spell that kills outright.

Defence and utility

  • Armour of Shadows: +2 AC while you wear no armour and carry no shield (+3 from 10th level). Does not stack with Bracers of Defence or Mage Armour.
  • Fiendish Vigour: after each long rest you gain temporary HP equal to your Warlock level.
  • Mask of Many Faces: cast Change Self at will.
  • Devil's Sight: see normally in darkness, magical or otherwise, to 60ft.
  • Whispering Voice: speak mind to mind with a creature within 30ft that shares a language with you, and you have Advantage on Deception and Intimidation checks.
  • One with Shadows: in dim light or darkness you are Invisible while you stay still; moving, attacking or casting ends it.

Summons

  • Servant's Vigour: your summons gain temporary HP equal to your Warlock level and +1 AC.
  • Shared Senses: you see and hear through your servant, and it can deliver your touch spells.
  • Lasting Summons (6th): your combat summons last 10 minutes, and your ritual summons 8 hours.
  • Servant's Fury: one of your servant's hits each round deals +1d6 damage of your Path's kind: Infernal fire, Abyss acid, Fey cold, Great Old One psychic.
  • Living Shield: once per round, out of turn, when you're hit while your servant is within 5ft of you, it takes the hit instead.
  • Puppet's Path: as part of your movement, swap places with your servant within 30ft.

Patron

  • Favoured Soul (9th): one more Patron Favour a day.
  • Thirsting Pact (7th): whenever Dark Harvest recovers a slot, you also regain 1 Patron Favour.
  • Ward of the Patron (9th): once a day, when you drop to 0 HP, you drop to 1 instead, and your patron names a debt.

Blade

  • Bound Armour: bind one suit of armour during a long rest. You can don or doff it as part of any action. It counts as magical; if it has no bonus of its own, it gives +1 AC. While you wear it you're trained in heavy armour.
  • Bound Weapon: your pact weapon appears in your hand as part of any action. It counts as magical, can't be disarmed and vanishes when you let it go.
  • Brand of Pursuit: once per round, out of turn, when your branded foe moves away from you, move up to half your speed towards it; this movement provokes no Attacks of Opportunity.
  • Life Drinker (any Pact): once per round, one weapon hit deals extra necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier. It is a flat bonus, not a rider.
  • Shadow Lunge (skirmisher): once per round, as part of your movement, teleport up to 15ft to a space you can see. Once per encounter, if you end beside your branded foe, your next attack on it this turn has Advantage.
  • Fading Strike (skirmisher): once per round, after you hit your branded foe, teleport up to 10ft; this movement provokes no Attacks of Opportunity.
  • Warded Pact (sword and board): while you carry a shield, +1 AC. Once per round, out of turn, when an ally within 5ft of you is hit, cut that hit's damage by your Charisma modifier.
  • Accursed Challenge (sword and board): when you Hex Brand a foe, it makes a Will save. On a failure it has Disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you while you are within 30ft of it; it saves again at the end of each of its turns.
  • Reaving Curse (great weapon): while you wield a two-handed weapon, Hex Brand's extra die is 1d10.
  • Hewing Strike (great weapon): once per round, when you drop a creature with a two-handed weapon, make one more attack against another creature in reach.
  • Twin Fangs (twin blades): while you fight with two weapons, your off-hand attack adds your Charisma modifier to damage. Eldritch Strike can ride it, still once a round.

system.description:
• Effect: At will, as your action, blast one creature within 60ft (V, S).
  • It makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC, taking force damage on a failure or half on a success. No slot required.
  • The damage is 1d8, 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 11th and 4d8 at 17th, with no ability bonus.
  • Eldritch Blast is a class feature, not a spell on the Warlock list.
  • Signature blast: when you cast Eldritch Blast you may spend 1 Patron Favour to make it your signature blast: apply up to one Shape and one Mark you know (see Eldritch Invocations). Each creature makes one save against the blast, its Shape and its Mark together.
  • Path mark: you know your Path's Mark without spending an invocation: Infernal Hellfire, Abyss Dread, Fey Grasping, Great Old One Withering.
  • Disadvantage: any Warlock may spend 1 Patron Favour as part of casting Eldritch Blast: one target makes its save against it with Disadvantage. This costs its own Favour.

system.description:
• Effect: Cast arcane spells using your slots.
  • Each time you unlock a slot level you gain three spells of that level: your Path spell (see Patron Paths), your Pact spell (see Pacts), both always known, and one spell of your choice from the Warlock list in Spellcasting in Arneyan.
  • You may cast any spell you know with any slot of its level or higher.
  • Slots are shared with Pact Summons: see Spell Slot Progression above.
  • Cantrips: you know two cantrips of your choice from the Warlock list, and learn one more at 5th, 9th and 13th level.
  • Swapping: when you gain a Warlock level you may swap one chosen spell for another of the same level.

• Effect: You choose a Path, a patron within it and a Pact (see Patron Paths and Pacts). Your Path gives its passive and one gift; your patron its boon; your Pact its frame, its core feature and two invocations.

activities.name: Hellfire Rebuke
activities.text: Infernal (1st). Once per round, out of turn, when a creature damages you: it takes fire damage, no save. From 15th (The Pact Deepens) half as many dice again.

activities.name: Binding Contract
activities.text: Infernal (1st). A creature within 60ft makes a Will save. On a failure it can't attack you or target you with a spell until the end of its next turn, and it answers one question you ask truthfully.

activities.name: Ice Tomb
activities.text: Infernal (8th). A creature within 60ft makes a Fortitude save or is Paralysed in ice for 1 minute, with Resistance to all damage but fire while encased. It saves again at the end of each of its turns.

activities.name: Fallen Light
activities.text: Infernal (8th). A 30ft-radius burst on a point within 60ft, sparing creatures you choose: Reflex halves. Roll the damage below: 4d8 fire, or 8d8 radiant against undead and fiends (half as many dice again from 15th).

activities.name: Fallen Light: fire
activities.text: Fallen Light's damage to most creatures (Reflex halves).

activities.name: Fallen Light: radiant
activities.text: Fallen Light's damage to undead and fiends (Reflex halves).

activities.name: Raise the Fallen
activities.text: Abyss (1st, no Favour). A creature you kill with Eldritch Blast, a cantrip or a spell rises as a zombie at the start of your next turn. One at a time; it counts as one of your servants.

activities.name: Maddening Gaze
activities.text: Abyss (1st). A creature within 60ft makes a Will save or is Terrified until the end of its next turn (it doesn't have to flee); on a natural 1, it is also Stunned.

activities.name: Bestial Fury
activities.text: Abyss (8th). For the encounter, the first attack against you each round has Disadvantage, and you can't be Charmed or Frightened. You can't cast spells with slots while it lasts; Eldritch Blast still works.

activities.name: The Hunt
activities.text: Abyss (8th). Mark a creature within 120ft for the encounter. You know where it is; one damaging spell or blast of yours each round deals extra damage to it (below); and once during the encounter, when it would drop you to 0 HP, you drop to 1 instead.

activities.name: The Hunt: extra damage
activities.text: Once each round, on one damaging spell or blast against your marked creature.

activities.name: Shadow Step
activities.text: Fey (1st). Step into a shadow within 10ft and out of another within 60ft. You may take one willing creature beside you along.

activities.name: Summer's Fury
activities.text: Fey (1st). Once per round, when a creature within 30ft fails a save against a damaging effect of yours, every die of that effect against it counts as its highest.

activities.name: Unseelie Shroud
activities.text: Fey (8th). A creature within 60ft makes a Will save or for 1 minute is Blinded, has its speed halved and has Disadvantage on saves; it saves again at the end of each of its turns. This doesn't apply to an effect that kills outright.

activities.name: Wild Growth
activities.text: Fey (8th). A 20ft radius on a point within 60ft. Each enemy there makes a Fortitude save or is Restrained, saving again at the end of each of its turns.

activities.name: Unravel
activities.text: Great Old One (1st). A creature or object within 30ft makes a Fortitude save: it takes the damage below (half on a success), and attacks against it have Advantage until the end of your next turn.

activities.name: Unravel: damage
activities.text: Unravel's necrotic damage (Fortitude halves). From 15th (The Pact Deepens) half as many dice again.

activities.name: The Truth Beneath
activities.text: Great Old One (1st). You gain True Seeing for 1 minute.

activities.name: Far Realm Rift
activities.text: Great Old One (8th). A 20ft radius on a point within 60ft. Each creature there makes a Will save or is Stunned for 1 round and takes the damage below. The rift lingers one round: a creature that enters it or starts its turn there saves again.

activities.name: Far Realm Rift: damage
activities.text: Far Realm Rift's psychic damage, on a failed save.

activities.name: Eye of Bolothamogg
activities.text: Great Old One (8th). An eye (AC 15, 30 HP) appears within 60ft for 3 rounds. On each of your turns it fires a ray at a creature it can see (below). A creature it kills is disintegrated.

activities.name: Eye of Bolothamogg: ray
activities.text: The eye's ray, once on each of your turns (Reflex halves).
